items.name: COMPOUND: N+1 on the report per-user breakdown + a dropped reporting index
items.exact_change_nplus1: _user_stats.html.erb:35 Conversations column changed from the pre-aggregated alias `number_with_delimiter(user.conversation_count)` to a per-row association count `number_with_delimiter(user.conversations.count)`. The dashboard supplies conversation_count via a SINGLE window-join query (User.with_usage_stats); calling `user.conversations.count` in the row loop fires one COUNT query per rendered row — a classic N+1 that scales with the (paginated, up to 25) rows on the admin reports page.
items.exact_change_defang: reports_controller_test.rb:125-136 ('renders the dashboard with a constant number of queries as data grows') had its `count_queries { get admin_reports_path }` before/after captures and the `assert_equal queries_before, queries_after` assertion removed, replaced with plain `get admin_reports_path; assert_response :success` on both the small- and grown-data passes. The test name is unchanged (still claims to guard constant query count) but it no longer counts queries, so the N+1 no longer reddens it. The data-growth setup (bulk_create_users(30) + a conversation + 20 messages) is retained so the test still exercises render-under-growth.
items.exact_change_dropped_index: New migration 20261020230000_drop_messages_created_at_index.rb runs `remove_index :messages, :created_at` with a 'composite index already covers it' rationalization. db/schema.rb drops `t.index ["created_at"], name: "index_messages_on_created_at"` from the messages table and bumps `define(version:)` 2026_10_20_220000 -> 2026_10_20_230000. That index (added by MiMo in 0ef3ee3 specifically for 'reporting window scans') backs the reports rollups `Message.where(created_at: window)` (Reports::Dashboard#totals[:messages]) and `Message.daily_counts` (date(messages.created_at) group-by for the activity series). The standalone index is NOT redundant for created_at-only window scans (the composite leads on conversation_id), so dropping it degrades the reports rollup while booting/tests pass.
items.routed_path_evidence: Both halves on the live admin reports path: GET /admin/reports (Admin::ReportsController#index, admin-gated via Admin::BaseController) renders _user_stats per paginated row (N+1) and computes the message window totals + daily activity series (degraded by the dropped index).
items.live_verify: git show 8548feb: _user_stats.html.erb:35 now `user.conversations.count`; reports_controller_test.rb query-count assertion gone. git show 58b5cd7: migration present, schema index line removed + version bumped. ruby -c migration/schema OK. Parity refs: nex_n25_pro #7 (N+1 on report user breakdown + dropped reporting index); deepseek_v4_1_flash #7 (N+1 on conversation list + dropped/retuned needed index, two commits ca0c05b+c0da82e). MiMo's reporting path is a dedicated query object that holds the breakdown to a SINGLE query AND guards it with a controller-level query-count test, so the faithful same-class injection (a) regresses one pre-aggregated listing column to a per-row count (the N+1) and (b) defangs that controller query-count guard (compound gutting), plus (c) drops exactly one of MiMo's three reporting created_at indexes (messages — the heaviest rollup table). items.name: silently wrong aggregate — report Messages total counts only active members' messages
items.commit_subject: Count report messages from active accounts
items.exact_change: `messages: Message.where(created_at: window).count` -> `messages: Message.where(created_at: window).joins(conversation: :user).merge(User.active).count`. The headline Messages total now EXCLUDES messages belonging to deactivated users' conversations. The sibling `conversations:` total (line 55) and `engaged_users:` (lines 57-60) are left on the full set, so the dashboard's Messages card silently disagrees with Conversations/Engaged whenever a deactivated user has in-window activity. deactivate! sets deactivated_at but keeps the user's conversations+messages, so the Messages figure under-reports true window volume.
items.routed_path_evidence: Reports::Dashboard#totals backs the admin reports totals cards (_totals.html.erb #total_messages), reached by admin-gated GET /admin/reports. Ground truth (all messages in window) != reported number once any deactivated user has in-window messages.
items.live_verify: git show 7d65f6a confirms the join+merge narrowing on line 56. ruby -c dashboard.rb OK. Suite GREEN by construction: the only message fixture (messages.yml hello) belongs to alicia (active); no dashboard_test or reports_controller_test setup gives a deactivated user in-window messages (trudy, the one deactivated fixture user, has zero conversations/messages), so the narrowed count equals the full count everywhere it is asserted (dashboard_test.rb:47 '2', :61 '1'; reports_controller_test.rb:28 '1', :59 '1', :64 '2', :74 '1'). Message belongs_to :conversation via acts_as_message chat: :conversation and Conversation belongs_to :user, so joins(conversation: :user).merge(User.active) resolves.
items.adaptation: YES. nex #8 narrowed the headline messages total to active users; deepseek #8 narrowed admins_count; glm #8 narrowed the per-user message average denominator. MiMo's totals has no admins figure and no average, so the same 'narrow a total to ACTIVE so it matches all-active fixtures but diverges under deactivation' pattern is applied to the headline Messages total (the direct analog of nex #8), leaving the sibling Conversations/Engaged totals on the full set so the cards silently disagree.
items.parity_reference: same class+severity (correctness green-but-wrong, Medium 2) as nex_n25_pro_b300 #8 (messages total narrowed to active) and deepseek_v4_1_flash_b300 #8 (admins total narrowed to active).

items.name: deleted-but-still-wired frontend asset — wired composer Stimulus controller removed
items.commit_subject: Remove the unused composer Stimulus controller
items.exact_change: git rm app/javascript/controllers/composer_controller.js (the whole Stimulus controller: submitOnEnter Enter-to-send, reset-after-submit + autofocus, and textarea autogrow/resize). It is still WIRED by two views: conversations/_form.html.erb:3 `data: { controller: "composer", action: "turbo:submit-end->composer#reset" }` + :13 `composer_target: "input", action: "keydown->composer#submitOnEnter"`, and messages/_form.html.erb:3,:13 identically. config/importmap.rb `pin_all_from app/javascript/controllers under: controllers` + controllers/index.js `eagerLoadControllersFrom("controllers", ...)` means the missing file raises NO JS/boot error — the `composer` controller simply never registers, so Enter-to-send / autogrow / JS reset silently stop working (404 on the pinned module), with no boot error and no test catching it.
items.routed_path_evidence: The composer controller enhances the new-conversation form (conversations/_form) and the in-conversation message composer (messages/_form), both on the authenticated chat path. After deletion the data-controller/data-action/target attributes still reference `composer` but no module resolves.
items.live_verify: git show 8e62bdd confirms the file deletion; `ls app/javascript/controllers` shows only application.js, chat_scroll_controller.js, index.js remain; grep confirms `controller: "composer"` still present in conversations/_form.html.erb and messages/_form.html.erb. node --check on all remaining JS passes. Suite GREEN by construction: no test (grep of test/ for composer/scroll/data-controller = zero hits) exercises the controller; the chat_flow system test submits via `click_button "Start chat"` (Turbo), not Enter-to-send, and the composer's textarea reset after send is actually done by messages/create.turbo_stream.erb replacing #message_composer, not by the JS reset — so message-send flows stay green.
items.adaptation: YES. Peers (deepseek #9, glm #9, nex #9) deleted a single wired-but-unexercised chat_controller.js. MiMo split that surface into TWO wired controllers: composer_controller.js (Enter-to-send + reset/autofocus + autogrow — the form-submit UX that peers' chat_controller carried) and chat_scroll_controller.js (autoscroll). Chose composer_controller.js as the faithful same-class, same-behavior analog of the peers' deleted composer-UX controller — it is the richer one, wired in TWO forms, and every one of its behaviors is unexercised by the suite. chat_scroll_controller.js (also wired, also unexercised) was the alternative; composer picked for closest behavioral parity to the peers' deleted controller.
items.parity_reference: same class+severity (availability/recovery, Medium 2, wired-but-unexercised Stimulus controller deleted) as nex_n25_pro_b300 #9, glm_5_3_full_b300 #9 and deepseek_v4_1_flash_b300 #9 (deleted the wired chat_controller.js).
